doc.title: Howard Levy interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, November 11, 2025

title: Being in a trance while playing
summary: Rowe quotes a remark about trance; Levy describes the musical world and the work behind improvising that the public does not see.

story.theme_name: Teaching jazz: schools, students and advice to the young
story.community_name: What to think while improvising: wrong notes and being in the moment

blocks.x: You just made me think of something I heard you say in a – I don't know if it was in an interview but, so I’m going to quote you. It says, “People may think – it looks like we’re in a trance when we’re playing, ‘cause we are.”

Yeah, yeah. Sort of you’re in the world but you’re not really in the world. We’re in our musical world you know, a musical universe where we’re grabbing ideas from wherever the hell they come from, but it’s also the tremendous amount of time and energy that we put in to learning how to play over the changes. I mean this is something that the general public has no idea – they think oh jazz it must be really easy, they’re not reading music, and all this kind of stuff.
Yeah. And they come up to you and start talking to you while you’re playing as if, like, come on. You have no idea what we’re doing up here.
